title: Data types

spans.text: Types determine how a program handles numbers, text, and collections. A number from a form begins as text and must be converted before arithmetic.

A type determines which operations a value supports and how it behaves. int represents integers, float uses binary floating point, str stores Unicode text, and bool represents True/False. list is mutable and ordered, tuple is immutable and ordered, set stores unique elements, and dict maps keys to values.

reveals the runtime type; isinstance is usually better for API checks. Ignoring types can cause TypeError, semantic bugs, or accidental mutation. float is a binary approximation; use Decimal for exact monetary arithmetic.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Do not calculate on unvalidated input; floats may not represent decimal fractions exactly and `int()` truncates.
Text, int, and float are different types; test conversion errors and floating-point precision explicitly.
